info.title: Skywake API
info.description: Branches of whole filesystems, and search indexes, for agents. Namespace, index and branch names may hold `/`; encode it as `%2F` in paths. Send `Authorization: Bearer <API key or token>`. Public namespaces can be read without one.

key.description: The first admin key, shown only this once.

error.description: What went wrong, for people to read.

request_id.description: The request's id, also in the `X-Request-Id` header. Quote it in bug reports.

path.description: For an invalid request, the JSON path of the field that is wrong.

ErrorBody.description: The body of every error response.

ErrorCode.description: What kind of error it is, for programs to check.

id.description: The id, when the console made the organization. Then no key is made: its people sign in.

cidrs.description: Addresses the organization's keys and console sessions may call from, as CIDRs such as `203.0.113.0/24` or `2001:db8::/32`; a lone address means only itself. Empty: any.

status.description: `open` for the month under way, which still grows.

lines.description: Per index and item; none for zero use.

quantity.description: Units used: GB-months of storage, GB written, TB scanned, texts, documents, GB-hours.

amount_cents.description: The quantity times the unit price, in cents, rounded.

InvoiceItem.description: What a line charges for. Storage is in GB-months: the size of `main` each day, over the days of the month. Writes are GB written. Queries are TB scanned: each query counts the size of the index it searched. Pinned is in GB-hours: the size of `main` for each hour of each replica; a pinned index's queries are not charged.

enabled.description: Whether this server bills at all.

usage_cents.description: The usage of the period so far.

estimate_cents.description: The usage or the minimum, whichever is more.

files.description: Bytes stored by the organization's filesystems.

customer.description: Whether the portal can be opened.

Plan.description: `unlimited` when the server does not bill, as when self-hosted.

PaidPlan.description: The plan the subscription moves to when the period ends.

amount_cents.description: What the quantity costs, before the minimum.

limit.description: The plan's monthly limit, if it has one.

CheckoutStart.description: A Stripe Checkout page to send the person to, or, with SKYWAKE_API_CHECKOUT=custom, a session the console confirms itself.

publishable_key.description: The Stripe key Stripe.js loads with.

required_domains.description: People with an email at these domains must sign in through the organization's single sign-on. Console tokens of theirs that did not come from it are refused.

orgs.description: The organizations whose people at this domain must use single sign-on.

namespaces.description: A namespace name, `<folder>/*` for every namespace under it, or `*`.

created_by.description: Who made the key: `user:<id>` for a person in the console, `key:<id>` for another key. Null for keys made before this was kept.

created_by_email.description: The email of the person who made it, when a person did.

Role.description: What a caller may do. `read`: files, history and sessions. `write`: also fork, commit, merge and start sessions. `admin`: also keys, namespaces, protected branches and the audit log.

key.description: The key. It is shown only this once.

namespaces.description: A namespace name, `<folder>/*` for every namespace under a folder, or `*` for all of them, the default.

expires_in_days.description: Whole days, 1 to 3650. Without it, the key does not expire. A key never outlives the key that makes it: it expires then at the latest.

id.description: Pass the last one as `after` for the next page.

org.description: The caller's organization; null before sign-in.

owner.description: The organization that owns what was used, when it is not the caller's.

actor.description: `key:ID` for an API key, the person's id for the console, or `admin` for the operator.

action.description: The operation, as in this document, such as `createBranch`.

resource.description: The route's parameters: the namespace, branch, index, path and so on.

chain.description: The API server that recorded it.

hash.description: sha256 of the event and `prev`, the hash of the event before it on `chain`: a changed or missing event breaks every hash after it.

AuditOutcome.description: `ok`; `denied` for lack of access (401, 403); `rejected` as a bad request (other 4xx); `error` on our side (5xx).

default.description: Used when no region is asked for.

EnvironmentStore.description: Your bucket, when the environment keeps its data there. Null: the server's.

principal.description: The AWS principal to trust in the role's trust policy.

externalId.description: The external ID the trust policy must require.

endpoint.description: An S3 compatible endpoint, such as R2's or MinIO's. AWS when not given.

Visibility.description: `private`: only the organization's keys and members. `public`: anyone may also read it, without a key, by naming it `<org>:<namespace>`.

region.description: Where its data lives. It can't change later. The default region if not given.

behind.description: Whether newer files wait to be indexed.

error.description: Why the last try failed, if it did.

index.description: The index to keep up with the files. Made when missing, with `path` and `text` attributes; an existing one must have both.

include.description: Globs of paths to index, such as `src/**`. All when empty.

exclude.description: Globs of paths never to index, such as `node_modules/**`.

maxBytes.description: Larger files are left out. 1 MiB when not given.

embed.description: Also embed each file (its first 8,000 characters) for vector search, when the index is made. Billed as embeddings.

store.description: The namespace's folder in the bucket, as `s3://<bucket>/<prefix>`.

endpoint.description: The S3 endpoint, for S3-compatible stores. Null for AWS.

expiresAt.description: Ask again before then. At least 15 minutes ahead.

nodes.description: The cache servers that own branch heads.

folder.description: The namespace's folder, as the cache servers name it.

pass.description: Sent as the bearer token. Good until `expiresAt`, for this folder and access only.

heads.description: When the cache servers own this namespace's branch heads: change heads through them. These credentials then cannot write `refs/`.

allOf.description: `write` needs a key with the `write` role.

protected.description: A protected branch changes only by merge.

from.description: The branch to fork. Without it, the new branch is empty.

at.description: Fork this older commit of `from` instead of its head.

withIndex.description: Also fork the linked index, from its version that matches the fork's commit, and keep it up with this branch. Needs `from` and a namespace with a linked index.

head.description: The commit the branch points to.

base.description: The newest commit this branch shares with `forked_from`: where it forked, or where the two last merged. What the branch changed since is `diff?from=<forked_from>&against=base`. Null for an empty branch, or once `forked_from` is deleted.

entries.description: What a folder holds, in name order. Empty for anything else.

modified.description: When a file last changed, in milliseconds since 1970. 0 otherwise.

head.description: The branch's head after the call.

changed.description: False when every change matched what was already there. Then no commit is made and `head` is the current one.

session.description: The session making the change. The commit records it.

parts.description: The new content: uploaded parts, in order.

at.description: Copy from this commit. By default, from the branch before this commit.

from.description: Copies the file, folder or symlink at `path`, without copying data. With a delete of `path` in the same commit, this is a move.

folder.description: Makes an empty folder, unless a folder is already there.

FileChange.description: One change. Give exactly one of `text`, `base64`, `parts`, `from`, `folder` or `delete`.

part.description: The BLAKE3 hash of the bytes, in hex.

merged.description: For a merge: the commit that was merged in.

path.description: A new or removed folder is one change, not one per file.

size.description: The file's size after this commit. Null if the commit deleted it.

head.description: The new head of `into`, when the merge landed.

conflicts.description: Paths changed on both sides in ways that do not combine.

error.description: What went wrong, for people to read.

request_id.description: The request's id, also in the `X-Request-Id` header. Quote it in bug reports.

into.description: The branch that receives the merge. It may be protected.

session.description: The session doing the merge. The merge commit records it.

dry_run.description: Only report the conflicts a merge would have now, less those `resolve` covers.

resolve.description: How to settle conflicts, by path. A path's resolution also settles the conflicts inside it. With every conflict covered, the merge lands as one merge commit with both parents.

take.description: `ours`: the path as it is on `into`. `theirs`: as it is on `from`.

parts.description: New content: uploaded parts, in order.

Resolution.description: What one conflicting path becomes. Give exactly one of `take`, `text`, `base64`, `parts` or `delete`.

error.description: What went wrong, for people to read.

session.description: The session making the change. The commit records it.

to.description: The commit whose files the branch should have.

read_only.description: Writes are refused while it is true.

retention_days.description: How long a branch's older versions stay to go back to, in days after they were replaced. Null keeps every one.

id.description: `uuid` makes every id a UUID, stored in 16 bytes: written as text with or without dashes in any case, and returned lowercase with dashes. Unset, an id is a string or a whole number. It can't change.

IndexSchema.description: The columns of an index. Attributes can be added later; vector columns can't change.

from.description: A string or text attribute. A document that gives no vector for this column gets its vector by embedding that attribute's text.

embed.description: Lets documents and queries give text for this vector: the server embeds it with `model` on its embedding provider. The model must give `dims` numbers.

Metric.description: How vectors are compared. Each is a distance, so smaller is closer: `1 - cos` for `cosine`, the squared distance for `euclidean`, the negative dot product for `dot`.

k1.description: BM25's term saturation for a `text` attribute. 1.2 by default.

b.description: BM25's length normalization for a `text` attribute. 0.75 by default.

stopwords.description: Whether a `text` attribute drops its language's stopwords, such as `the` and `of`. False by default, so phrases like `to be or not to be` work.

stemming.description: Whether a `text` attribute matches words by their stem, so `running` finds `run`. True by default.

filterable.description: Whether a `text` attribute also filters, orders and groups by its whole value, like a string. False by default.

case_sensitive.description: Whether a `text` attribute tells `Apple` from `apple`. False by default.

ascii_folding.description: Whether `café` in a `text` attribute matches `cafe`. False by default.

max_token_length.description: Longer words in a `text` attribute are left out. 39 by default.

pre_tokenized.description: Whether a `text` attribute is a list of strings, each one word as it is, not split or changed.

filter_index.description: Also keeps the documents sorted by this attribute, so a vector query whose filter passes few documents reads just those. For one value, not a list, `sparse` or `vectors`. It can be turned on later and is built by the next build.

AttributeType.description: `int` is a whole number. `uuid` and `datetime` are written and read as strings; a `datetime` is RFC 3339 (or a date, or milliseconds since 1970) and comes back in UTC. `strings`, `ints` and `numbers` are lists; a filter holds if it holds for any item. `text` is a string searched by BM25: split into words, lowercased and stemmed in its `language`. `sparse` is `{indices, values}`, as SPLADE writes, and `vectors` a list of vectors of one length, as ColBERT writes; both are scored by `rank`, never filtered or ordered by.

TextLanguage.description: The stemming language of a `text` attribute. `english` by default.

kms_key_id.description: A key id or ARN in your cloud's key service. Every object of the index is encrypted with it; revoking the key there makes the data unreadable.

replicas.description: Servers that keep the index open and on their disks.

IndexPinned.description: Reserved servers for the index, billed per GB-hour for each replica instead of per query. Queries go to the least busy replica. A copy is not pinned.

region.description: Where its data lives. It can't change later. The default region if not given.

shards.description: The parts documents are split over by id, each written and searched in parallel. More suits more data and writes; it can't change later.

unindexed_rows.description: Rows written since the last build, scanned exactly.

IndexStats.description: Of the `main` branch. Null while the server cannot count them.

replicas.description: The replicas placed; fewer than asked while fewer servers run.

IndexPinning.description: Where it is pinned; null if it is not.

server.description: The API server holding the replica.

warm.description: Whether every object of the current version is on the server's disk.

retention_days.description: Days a version stays after it was replaced; `collect` deletes older ones. Null keeps every version.

attributes.description: Attributes to add. One the index has must keep its type, but can turn on `filter_index`. Documents written before lack the new ones.

drop_attributes.description: Attributes to take out, with their values. One may come back later only as it was. Refused while the index has more than one branch, as they share its data.

region.description: Where the copy's data lives. The source index's region if not given.

allOf.description: The new index's key; none by default.

target_org.description: Another organization to make the new index in. Needs a console token of someone with write access in both; an API key belongs to one organization.

at.description: Fork this older version of `from` instead of its head.

time.description: When the branch came to be like this.

IndexVersion.description: A branch at one moment of its history.

version.description: The version to go back to.

from.description: The branch whose writes are added.

upserted_ids.description: With `returnAffectedIds`: the ids written, by an upsert.

deleted_ids.description: With `returnAffectedIds`: the ids deleted, by a delete.

allOf.description: What this request counted toward the bill.

DocId.description: A string, or a whole number from 0; a UUID when the schema's `id` is `uuid`.

returnAffectedIds.description: Also return the ids the write changed, one for each count. Off by default.

vectors.description: A vector for every vector column of the schema. A column with `embed` also takes text, or an image, which the server embeds.

Image.description: An image for a column with `embed`, as an https URL or a base64 `data:image/...` URL. Its model must take images.

AttributeValue.description: An object's fields are attributes of their own: `{author: {name}}` is `author.name`.

vectors.description: A vector for every vector column of the schema. A column with `embed` also takes text, or an image, which the server embeds.

next.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page. Null on the last page.

deleted.description: Only ids that were there count.

deleted_ids.description: With `returnAffectedIds`: the ids deleted, as `deleted` counts them.

allOf.description: What this request counted toward the bill.

patches.description: A patch of a missing document does nothing.

allOf.description: Keyword objects: `{and: [..]}`, `{or: [..]}`, `{not: ..}`, or `{<attribute>: {<op>: value}}` with op `eq`, `ne`, `in`, `not_in`, `lt`, `lte`, `gt` or `gte`; on a list, `contains_all` and `contains_any`; on a string, `glob`, `iglob` (any case), `regex` and `fuzzy` (`{"text": "..", "edits": 0 to 2, "ignoreCase": false}`, a whole value within that many edits, a swap of two letters counting as one). `exists: true` holds when a document has the attribute and `exists: false` when it does not. `{id: {..}}` filters by document id with `eq`, `ne`, `in`, `not_in`, or `lt`, `lte`, `gt` and `gte` in id order, which pages through every document. Many keys in one object must all hold. A document without the attribute fails every comparison. On a list, an op holds if it holds for any item. In `search`, a `text` attribute takes `phrase` (these words, in order), `prefix` (the same, the last word a prefix), `contains_all_tokens` (every word, anywhere) or `contains_any_token` (at least one word), at the top or inside `and`. Words are analyzed as the attribute is: lowercased, stemmed, without stopwords if it drops them. A `filterable` text attribute also takes the ops of a string, on its whole value.

returnAffectedIds.description: Also return the ids the write changed, one for each count. Off by default.

Write.description: One change, in this order: `deleteBy`, `patchBy`, `upserts`, `patches`, `deletes`. Its conditions see exactly the documents it replaces: if another write lands first, it is worked out again.

Condition.description: A filter checked against each document as it was before the write; a missing one has no attributes. A value may be `{"$ref_new": "<attribute>"}`, that attribute of the document being written.

distance.description: Smaller is closer, for every metric.

rerank_score.description: With `rerank`, the model's score: larger is better.

cache_temperature.description: `hot`: everything came from memory; `warm`: some from the disk cache; `cold`: some from object storage.

cache_hit_ratio.description: The share of reads a cache served, from 0 to 1.

vector.description: `value` may be text when the column has `embed`.

recall.description: The share of the true nearest `topK` to find, from 0 to 1. probe.description: Clusters to read, instead of what `recall` needs. More is slower and finds more of the true nearest.

field.description: The `string` or `text` attribute whose value is ranked against `query`.

query.description: What to rank by. The search's text by default; a vector query needs it unless its vector is text.

topN.description: The most hits to return after reranking. Every hit by default.

fields.description: The text attributes to search. Every one by default.

boosts.description: A weight per field; 1 when missing.

fuzzy.description: Also match words within this many edits of each word searched for: a letter added, removed or changed, or two swapped. 0 by default.

fuse.description: Reciprocal rank fusion: a hit scores the sum of `weight / (k + rank)` over the searches that found it, ranks from 1. Weights are 1 when missing.

allOf.description: Reranks the fused hits. `query` is the first text search's by default, then the first vector given as text.

Hybrid.description: `rank` scores the hits the searches found instead of `fuse`; each search's `topK` is still how deep it looks.
